2. STEP 1 — INDEPENDENT DESIGN CLASSIFICATION & TOOL SELECTION (`RISK_OF_BIAS.md` §1):
   Classify the study's actual design from its Methods section, then select the matching appraisal tool:
   - `"RoB 2 (parallel-trial variant)"`: Individually randomized controlled trial. Rate all 5 domains (`D1` Randomization process; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"RoB 2 (cluster-randomized trials variant)"`: Cluster-randomized trial (villages, compounds, neighbourhoods, schools, utilities randomized as clusters). Rate all 6 domains (`D1a` Randomization process; `D1b` Timing of identification or recruitment of participants within clusters; `D2` Deviations from intended interventions; `D3` Missing outcome data; `D4` Measurement of the outcome; `D5` Selection of the reported result) as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`, and overall rating as `"Low"`, `"Some concerns"`, or `"High"`.
   - `"ROBINS-I"`: Non-randomized study of an intervention / policy with a genuine comparator (DiD, IV, RDD, PSM, ITS, controlled before-after, comparative longitudinal/panel evaluation). Rate all 7 domains (`D1` Bias due to confounding; `D2` Bias in selection of participants into the study; `D3` Bias in classification of interventions; `D4` Bias due to deviations from intended interventions; `D5` Bias due to missing data; `D6` Bias in measurement of outcomes; `D7` Bias in selection of the reported result — note `No information` honestly if no pre-analysis plan/protocol exists) as `"Low"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Serious"`, `"Critical"`, or `"No information"`, and overall rating in the same vocabulary. Do NOT assign single-case histories with no comparator arm to ROBINS-I!
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross Sectional Studies"`: Quantitative cross-sectional survey / observational regression without a quasi-experimental intervention structure. Rate all 8 items (`Q1` Inclusion criteria in sample clearly defined; `Q2` Study subjects and setting described in detail; `Q3` Exposure measured validly and reliably; `Q4` Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of condition; `Q5` Confounding factors identified; `Q6` Strategies to deal with confounding factors stated; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly and reliably; `Q8` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`. Provide overall narrative judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, or `"High concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies"`: Observational comparative cohort design (not framed as a ROBINS-I intervention). Rate all 11 items (`Q1` Similar groups from same population; `Q2` Exposures measured similarly; `Q3` Exposure measured validly/reliably; `Q4` Confounding factors identified; `Q5` Strategies to deal with confounding stated; `Q6` Participants free of outcome at start; `Q7` Outcomes measured validly/reliably; `Q8` Follow-up time reported and sufficient; `Q9` Follow-up complete or loss explored; `Q10` Strategies to address incomplete follow-up utilized; `Q11` Appropriate statistical analysis used) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, `"Unclear"`, or `"Not applicable"`, plus narrative overall judgment (`"Low concern"`, `"Some concern"`, `"High concern"`).
   - `"CASP Qualitative Checklist"`: Primary qualitative study (interviews, ethnography, focus groups, qualitative documentary/field case study). Rate all 10 items (`Q1` Clear statement of aims; `Q2` Qualitative methodology appropriate; `Q3` Research design appropriate to address aims; `Q4` Recruitment strategy appropriate to aims; `Q5` Data collected in a way that addressed research issue; `Q6` Relationship between researcher and participants adequately considered [reflexivity]; `Q7` Ethical issues considered; `Q8` Data analysis sufficiently rigorous; `Q9` Clear statement of findings; `Q10` How valuable is the research [narrative assessment]). Rate Q1-Q9 `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`, and Q10 narratively; give narrative `overall_rating` (e.g. `"Low methodological concern"`, `"Moderate concern (X Can't tell / No items)"`, `"High methodological concern"` — no numeric score).
   - `"MMAT (Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool)"`: Genuine mixed-methods primary study combining qualitative AND quantitative empirical components (do NOT assign purely quantitative or purely qualitative studies to MMAT). Rate Screening `S1`-`S2`, Qualitative `1.1`-`1.5`, the matching Quantitative 5-item block (`2.1`-`2.5` randomized, `3.1`-`3.5` non-randomized, or `4.1`-`4.5` descriptive), AND Mixed-Methods integration `5.1`-`5.5` (`5.1` adequate rationale for mixed methods; `5.2` components effectively integrated; `5.3` outputs of integration adequately interpreted; `5.4` divergences/inconsistencies adequately addressed; `5.5` components adhere to quality criteria of each tradition) as `"Yes"`, `"No"`, or `"Can't tell"`. Per MMAT 2018 rules, NEVER compute a numeric score; provide a concise criterion-grounded narrative `overall_rating` noting that overall quality cannot exceed the weakest component.
   - `"AMSTAR 2"`: Secondary systematic review, meta-analysis, or scoping review with an explicit systematic search/screening method (NEVER apply AMSTAR 2 to non-systematic narrative literature reviews!). Rate all 16 items `Q1`-`Q16` (explicitly marking critical domains `Q2`, `Q4`, `Q7`, `Q9`, `Q11`, `Q13`, `Q15`) as `"Yes"`, `"Partial Yes"` (where applicable), `"No"`, or `"Not applicable (no meta-analysis)"`, and apply AMSTAR 2 overall confidence (`"High"`, `"Moderate"`, `"Low"`, `"Critically Low"`).
   - `"Legal Institutional Evidence Appraisal Framework"`: Doctrinal-empirical hybrid, jurimetric analysis, or institutional/legal-historical case study that fits NONE of the six conventional designs above. Rate all 13 narrative domains (`D1` Legal source accuracy; `D2` Jurisdictional specificity; `D3` Exposure definition; `D4` Outcome definition; `D5` Sampling transparency; `D6` Selection process; `D7` Measurement transparency; `D8` Causal identification; `D9` Treatment of confounding; `D10` Institutional context; `D11` Replication potential; `D12` Coding transparency; `D13` Researcher reflexivity) as `"strong"`, `"adequate"`, `"weak"`, or `"not assessable"`. Explicitly frame `overall_rating` as a structured non-validated judgment (NEVER a numeric composite score!).
   - `"NONE"`: Use when the study fits NONE of the listed instruments (e.g., pure mathematical/simulation optimization model with no empirical sample, or non-systematic narrative essay/review with no primary empirical method and no systematic search). Set `overall_rating = "NOT APPLICABLE (design fits no listed tool)"`, explain clearly in `why_tool_chosen` and `overall_narrative_summary` rather than forcing an inappropriate checklist, and still fill the 7 `cross_tool_domains` honestly from the paper!

raw_response.chosen_tool: JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies

cross_tool_domains.attrition: Moderate concern: A balanced 7-year panel of 290 cities (2008-2014) equals 2,030 city-years, yet estimation samples drop to 1,769 (283 cities) for green space, 1,730-1,737 (282-283 cities) for wastewater, and 1,577-1,589 (276 cities; 22.3% missing city-years and 14 omitted cities) for solid waste (Tables 2-3, PDF pp. 8-9). Reasons for missing cities/years are not explained and listwise deletion is used without sensitivity or imputation checks.
cross_tool_domains.confounding: Moderate concern: Two-way fixed effects (city and year fixed effects) control for time-invariant municipal characteristics and common national shocks, alongside five time-varying socioeconomic/demographic covariates (GRP per capita, municipal spending per capita, high school/college enrollment proxy, registered unemployment rate, and population density) and restriction to pre-2014 to avoid the 2014 hukou reform (PDF pp. 5, 7-9). However, time-varying unobserved confounders (e.g., rapid industrialization or land-finance shifts driving both migrant inflows and per-capita infrastructure lag) remain possible, adult education is proxied by age 15-22 school/college enrollment (Note 4, PDF p. 12), and 3-year lagged estimates are null (PDF p. 10).
cross_tool_domains.legal_measurement_quality: Weak-to-moderate: While China's hukou household registration system is discussed conceptually in detail (PDF pp. 4-5), the empirical analysis does not directly code or measure city-level or temporal variation in hukou legal rules, conversion quotas, or administrative entitlements. Instead, hukou-based institutional exclusion is proxied solely by the demographic percentage of public-security-registered >1-year temporary residents in each city (PDF p. 6).
cross_tool_domains.measurement_bias: Moderate-to-high concern: Exposure and outcomes come from standardized national yearbooks (PDF pp. 5-7), avoiding recall bias, but suffer from proxy and scaling biases: (1) temporary resident counts include only migrants residing >1 year who registered with public security authorities, omitting unregistered and short-term (<1 year) rural migrants and conflating all non-local temporary residents with rural mingong (PDF p. 6); (2) city-wide infrastructure totals cannot capture intra-city spatial access for migrant neighborhoods (PDF pp. 6, 11); and (3) total urban population (permanent + temporary) sits in the denominator of both the focal exposure (% temporary residents) and all per-capita outcomes (Table 1 Note 1, PDF p. 7), creating mechanical denominator dilution during rapid migrant inflows.
cross_tool_domains.outcome_measurement_quality: Moderate: Wastewater treatment capacity (10,000 m3/day per 10,000 persons), annual wastewater volume treated (10,000 m3 per 10,000 persons), solid waste treatment capacity (tons/day per 10,000 persons), annual solid waste treated (10,000 tons per 10,000 persons), and public green space (ha per 10,000 persons) come from official China Urban Construction Statistical Yearbooks (Table 1, PDF pp. 6-7). However, prefecture-level per-capita facility metrics cannot measure household sewer connectivity, actual service delivery to migrant enclaves, or treatment quality (PDF pp. 6, 11).
cross_tool_domains.reporting_bias: Low-to-moderate concern (no preregistration reported): No pre-analysis plan or protocol is mentioned (Can't tell for formal pre-specification), but reporting across tested outcomes and sensitivity analyses is transparent, including prominent reporting of null results for public green space (Model 1, Table 3, PDF p. 9) and null 3-year lag specifications referenced in supplemental Tables A1-A5 (PDF p. 10).
cross_tool_domains.selection_bias: Moderate concern: Sampling covers nearly the universe of China's prefecture-level cities (290 cities from 2008 to 2014) from national administrative yearbooks (PDF p. 5), avoiding ad hoc case selection. However, unaddressed exclusion of 7-14 cities and 13%-22% of city-years due to missing yearbook data (Tables 2-3, PDF pp. 8-9) and reliance on public-security-registered >1-year temporary residents (excluding unregistered migrants) introduce potential selection/coverage bias.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Was the exposure measured in a valid and reliable way?
domain_ratings.justification: Although drawn from official statistical yearbooks, 'temporary residents' only counts individuals living away from their permanent address for over one year who are officially registered with local public security authorities. This systematically misses unregistered rural migrants and short-term (<1 year) floating workers, conflates all non-hukou temporary residents with disadvantaged rural migrant laborers (mingong), and proxies hukou institutional exclusion via demographic share rather than measuring local hukou rules directly.

domain_ratings.domain_name: Were the outcomes measured in a valid and reliable way?
domain_ratings.justification: Outcomes come from standardized national China Urban Construction Statistical Yearbooks, providing consistent engineering metrics of city-wide capacity and treated volume. However, as the authors acknowledge, prefecture-wide aggregates cannot verify whether local migrant communities actually benefit from or have spatial access to treatment infrastructure, and normalizing city-wide infrastructure by total population (permanent + temporary) mechanically couples the outcome denominator to temporary population inflows.

domain_ratings.justification: The 7-year observation period (2008-2014) and 1-, 2-, and 3-year lag specifications are clearly reported, but municipal planning, financing, and construction of wastewater and solid waste plants typically span multiple years; the disappearance of statistical significance in the 3-year-lag model leaves it unclear whether the timeframe captures deliberate policy underprovision versus short-run adjustment lags behind rapid migration inflows.

domain_ratings.justification: No missing-data strategies (such as multiple imputation, inverse-probability weighting, or balanced-panel sensitivity checks) are reported; estimations rely on complete-case listwise deletion across unbalanced panels.

domain_ratings.justification: Two-way fixed-effects panel models with city-clustered standard errors, Hausman specification tests, log transformations of skewed covariates, VIF diagnostics (1.73-1.78), lagged specifications, and 2008-2014 change regressions are appropriate econometric tools for city-year panel data. Nonetheless, placing total urban population (permanent + temporary) in both the denominator of % temporary residents and the denominator of per-capita infrastructure outcomes without separately controlling for total population creates a risk of mechanical ratio/denominator dilution during short-run population surges.

raw_response.overall_narrative_summary: Overall judgment: Some concern (JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies; no numeric score computed). Zhou and Liang (2021) analyze a 7-year longitudinal panel of 290 Chinese prefecture-level cities (2008-2014) from national statistical yearbooks using two-way (city and year) fixed-effects regressions, city-clustered standard errors, lagged predictor models, and 2008-2014 change regressions to test whether cities with a higher share of temporary residents provide lower per-capita public green space, wastewater treatment, and solid waste treatment infrastructure. Methodological strengths include nationwide administrative coverage, restriction to pre-2014 to avoid confounding from the 2014 State Council hukou reform, two-way fixed effects absorbing time-invariant city heterogeneity and national macro shocks, and transparent reporting of null results for green space and 3-year lags. However, substantial methodological concerns temper causal and environmental-justice inferences: (1) hukou institutional exclusion is not directly measured by local legal rules, but proxied by public-security-registered >1-year temporary residents (omitting unregistered and short-term rural migrants); (2) prefecture-wide outcomes cannot verify intra-city service access in migrant neighborhoods; (3) total urban population (permanent + temporary) appears in the denominator of both the focal exposure and all per-capita outcomes, risking mechanical short-run denominator dilution when migrant populations surge (consistent with the null 3-year lag estimates); and (4) 13%-22% of city-years (and 7-14 cities) are missing across regression models without explanation or missing-data handling.
raw_response.study_design_identified: Observational longitudinal panel (cohort) study of 290 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2008 to 2014 using two-way fixed-effects regressions, 1- to 3-year lagged models, and 7-year change regressions
raw_response.where_found_summary: Abstract (PDF p. 2 / p. 781); Data, measures, and methods — Data and sample, Environmental amenities and infrastructure, Migrant workers, Control variables, Models, and Table 1 (PDF pp. 5-8 / pp. 784-787); Results and Tables 2-3 (PDF pp. 8-10 / pp. 787-789); Discussion and conclusion & Notes 1-4 (PDF pp. 10-12 / pp. 789-791).
raw_response.why_tool_chosen: The study tracks a longitudinal panel (cohort) of 290 Chinese prefecture-level cities across seven annual waves (2008-2014), estimating within-city associations over time via two-way fixed-effects models, 1- to 3-year lagged exposure models, and 2008-2014 change models. ROBINS-I was not chosen because the study does not evaluate a discrete policy intervention or comparator arm—in fact, the authors explicitly restricted the sample to 2008-2014 to exclude the 2014 State Council hukou reform and characterize their design as examining observational correlations with a continuous demographic share (% temporary residents). JBI Analytical Cross-Sectional was not chosen because the primary design is longitudinal city-year panel follow-up rather than a single cross-section. JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Cohort Studies therefore best matches this observational longitudinal panel design.
